beats.text: A dying king's will started a world war. Britain still keeps the prize.
Charles the Second, the last Habsburg king of Spain, died with no children. Everyone wanted his empire.
His will left it all to a French prince: Philip, grandson of Louis the Fourteenth. Louis said yes.
France and Spain under one family? England, the Dutch and Austria went to war to stop it.
They backed a rival king, Archduke Charles of Austria. Spain itself split in two.
An Anglo-Dutch fleet took Gibraltar, in the archduke's name. The British kept it for themselves.
At Almansa, Philip's army won the decisive battle. Then he punished the kingdoms that had fought him, and abolished their old laws.
Peace came at Utrecht. Philip kept Spain, but lost Italy and the Netherlands. Britain got Gibraltar and Minorca.
Barcelona fought on alone, and fell on the eleventh of September. Catalonia still marks that day.
Philip became Spain's first Bourbon king. The king of Spain today, Felipe the Sixth, is his descendant.
And Gibraltar? Still British, three hundred years later.
